title: CyberMP archive mod compatibility
sectionTitle: Confirm compatibility one step at a time
plainText: Stage Evidence to record ------ 1. Baseline Record game, DLC and CyberMP builds, enabled core files and declared mod dependencies. Use a clean client without a manually installed copy of the tested asset. 2. Delivery Compare the packaged resource and the downloaded file by name and hash. Record whether delivery used the server or CDN. 3. Engine loading Record the resolved asset, named appearance, streamed block or TweakDB record, with the relevant client log or visible result. Add one companion file or loader feature at a time. 4. Local behavior Exercise the feature from the normal resource entry point. Check cleanup, rejoin and another cold launch where relevant. 5. Multiplayer behavior Run on two clients with the same required files. Check visibility, state changes, late join and streaming where the feature requires replication. For a client-local feature, verify the expected local scope. Report the last stage with positive evidence when a stage fails. For a dependency with unknown availability, record the observed failure and the specific API, record or asset still needed. This comparison lets an agent choose between reusing the existing asset and porting the mod's behavior to CyberMP resource code.

title: Object Spawning & World Streaming Reference
plainText: CyberMP provides two distinct mechanisms for spawning world objects, each suited for different use cases. Feature Client-Local (mp.local.spawnObject) Server-Authoritative (mp.objects.create) --------- Environment Client (@cybermp/client-types) Server (@cybermp/server-types) Network Replication Local to the executing client Streamed to eligible clients in range and in the assigned dimension Network Cost Zero bandwidth / RPC overhead Synchronized state updates Removal Pass the local handle to mp.local.despawnObject when done or on resource stop Destroy the object through prop.destroy() or mp.objects.destroy when the server resource no longer needs it Use Cases Decorative props, personal garage previews, client-only VFX markers, temporary scene staging Shared barricades, public furniture, racing tracks, custom buildings, drops A user-run base-game prop test on 21 November 2026 confirmed shared visibility on two clients, visibility after a late connection, and removal on both clients when the resource stopped. In the subsequent streaming test, the same live server object kept its Network ID, mp.network.getObjectGameId(networkId) returned 0 outside streaming, and returning assigned a new local Game ID. Treat that ID as a temporary client-side mapping: resolve it again after objectStreamIn rather than caching it across objectStreamOut. Filter both events by the tracked Network ID; their arguments are (netID, gameID). These observations cover the tested base-game asset and stand, not custom archive delivery or all game builds. See the portable probe and audit. ---

title: Build and load an archive prop
guideTitle: Build and load an archive prop
plainText: 1. Create a WolvenKit project named cybermp_kit_cube. Add a simple non-skinned single-submesh mesh container from a local game installation, or use one you have permission to redistribute. Copy it to cybermp_kit\diagnostics\cube.mesh in the project. Choose a clearly visible opaque material and check its dependencies. Keep all original game files in the author's local game installation as the source for any required template and record the template path used. 2. Generate the input with python3 make-cube.py cube.glb. Place the file under the matching raw path cybermp_kit/diagnostics/cube.glb. Use WolvenKit's Import/Export tool to import into cube.mesh. The generator writes one triangulated submesh with normals, UV coordinates and tangents. Check the log and mesh preview. Confirm that the selected mesh container has a compatible material slot. 3. Create or derive a simple static entity at cybermp_kit\diagnostics\cube.ent. Use a mesh component which references cube.mesh. If the selected entity uses appearances, include the necessary resources and record the tested appearance name. Verify references in WolvenKit. The example uses the default appearance candidate 0. Replace it with the appropriate CName hash if the chosen entity needs a named appearance. Record that change with the generated asset. 4. Pack and inspect cybermp_kit_cube.archive. Confirm the entity and mesh use the expected depot paths. Make a local single-player test installation and spawn the entity by its depot path using a suitable tool such as World Builder. Record the tool and version. Remove that local test installation from the CyberMP test environment before checking resource delivery. Sources. WolvenKit mesh import · WolvenKit project layout · World Builder custom resource inspection.

description: Add a single diagnostic widget and check geometry, color, and world projection independently.
plainText: Diagnostic for an INK minimap shape The typed client example creates one screen-space inkCircleWidget in the minimap controller's root widget by default. It discovers an existing controller through INK layer game controllers and also registers OnInitialize observers. It creates the child with container.AddChild('inkCircleWidget'), sets size through Vector2, and tint through HDRColor. It removes its own widget on resource stop and before replacing it. On 21 November 2026, a user-run test confirmed a visible yellow square in root and its disappearance after the server stopped only minimap-diagnostic, with the server continuing to run. The same example did not produce a visible shape in mappin or geom. This is one stand's result, not universal compatibility. Game executable FileVersion was 3.0.5813403; exact in-game CyberMP client and server builds remain unconfirmed. See the audit record for evidence and limits. There is no world-coordinate projection in this example.

plainText: 1. Record the game build, CyberMP client and server builds, and the kit revision. Confirm that either the observer fires or the existing-controller lookup succeeds. 2. title: Player spawn and health diagnostics
plainText: Register lifecycle observation before issuing the request. mp.local.spawnPlayer(...) returning true means the request started. It does not establish puppet availability, health initialization or world collision. Observe mp.game.onLocalPlayerSpawned, resolve the current puppet and verify the active request before follow-up native calls. See player mechanics and the official lifecycle guide.
